findings.evidence: The old `child -> source` MERGED_INTO edges stay in the graph store, and per the description the projection rebuild derives both edges from consolidation_log; every MERGED_INTO reader in src/ is asserted to tolerate multiple or stale out-edges, but that code is not visible in the diff. Check each ME
findings.title: Correctness of retained stale child->source edges depends on readers outside the diff

findings.evidence: If decisions.status has terminal states other than 'superseded' (e.g. deleted/archived; the enum is not visible in the diff), the predicate `status != 'superseded'` still accepts them for supersession. Verify the status enum only distinguishes supersede-eligibility by 'superseded'.
findings.title: Other non-superseded statuses remain supersedable

findings.evidence: After the authoritative commit the job performs N+1 graph relation writes (source plus each child), each preceded by authorization revalidation; a failure mid-loop propagates to the caller although the merge is committed. This extends a pre-existing post-commit pattern to N edges, and nothing in the
findings.title: Post-commit child graph writes can fail after the merge is durable

findings.evidence: The repointed audit loop issues one log_action_in_session per child inside the transaction and one post-commit graph write plus revalidation per child; acceptable at consolidation scale but a batch path may be worth checking against typical child counts.
findings.title: Per-child audit inserts and graph writes are O(N) round trips

findings.evidence: If `_cleanup_postgres` (defined outside the diff) deletes only the decision rows it is handed, the audit rows written by these merges (merged/repointed) linger in the shared database after teardown; check which tables it clears, since the fixture does not collect consolidation_log ids.
findings.title: Fixture cleanup may leave consolidation_log rows behind

findings.evidence: test_returns_confirmation_string and test_converts_old_decision_id_string_to_uuid now pass project_key='brain-v42', but the tool diff does not obviously make project_key mandatory; if a sub-path (e.g. plan_extracted_claims or persist_extracted_claims) rejects None, the unscoped tool path would depen
findings.title: Unexplained project_key requirement added to existing supersede tests

findings.evidence: DecisionNotSupersedableError(ValueError) covers both a nonexistent id and an already-superseded one, and the MCP tool returns the same message text for both; callers cannot distinguish a lookup failure from a state refusal. Cosmetic given the previous silent-success behavior was worse.
findings.title: Missing and already-superseded decisions are conflated

findings.evidence: The update predicate is id plus status with no project_key, so a caller may supersede another project's decision. Deliberate per the measured data (2 of 56 rows, project renames) and tracked in ticket 80a22743; listed so the authorization surface stays visible to the operator decision.
findings.title: Cross-project supersession remains allowed by design

findings.evidence: test_supersede_filters_old_decision_by_status_only asserts on rendered fragments of str(statement) ('WHERE', 'decisions.status !=', 'RETURNING decisions.id'), which depend on SQLAlchemy rendering; compile-params-based assertions (used elsewhere in the same test) are sturdier.
findings.title: SQL-string assertions are brittle

findings.evidence: In _update_merge_pair, target_update and source_update explicitly update updated_at=sa.text('NOW()'), but child_update only sets merged_into=target_id without updating updated_at.
findings.title: Child repointing update does not set updated_at timestamp

findings.evidence: In supersede, update_stmt filters on decisions.c.status != 'superseded'. In SQL ternary logic, if a decision row has status IS NULL, NULL != 'superseded' evaluates to UNKNOWN/false, preventing supersede of unscoped or default-null status records unless status is non-nullable.
findings.title: Status predicate decisions.c.status != 'superseded' excludes NULL status rows in SQL
